data.name: Imra
data.gender_notes: Imra is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'amr' meaning 'to command'. A name for one who is free and unbound. The name Imra carries the meaning “Free, Unrestrained” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Imra usually hope their child will grow to embody free, unrestrained and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Imra is a name that is deeply rooted in Islamic spirituality. It is said to represent the beauty and grace of the moon and the fragrance and elegance of jasmine. It is a name that is sure to inspire a sense of wonder and awe in those who hear it.
data.etymology: Imra belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, Unrestrained.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imra total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_urdu.name: عمیرہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: عمیرہ ایک علم مؤنث نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، اور عمر یا زندگی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، قرآن مجید میں آل عمران سورة کی 144 آية میں ذکر ہوا ہے، اور عمیر عمر کا تصغیر ہے، یہ نام بعض عرب ممالک میں مقبول ہے

in_english.name: Imra
in_english.meaning: A feminine given name meaning age or lifetime
in_english.long_meaning: Imra is a feminine given name of Arabic origin, meaning age or lifetime. It is mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al Imran, verse 144. The name is derived from the Arabic root 'umr', which signifies life or age. Historically, the name Imra has been used in various Arabic-speaking countries and holds spiritual significance as a reminder of the fleeting nature of life. The name is associated with virtues such as gratitude, patience, and mindfulness. In modern times, Imra remains a popular choice among Muslim parents worldwide, symbolizing a connection to their cultural and religious heritage.
